_doc: The release index of every maker whose namespace the catalog already resolves.
This answers a question no other check can. `check:upstream` asks whether an archived number
moved; the namespace watch in report:gaps asks whether a provider started *serving* a model.
Neither looks at the page where a maker publishes its benchmark table. Qwen3.8 Max was served,
detected and filed in the gaps issue on 2026-08-03 while its ~80-benchmark release table went
unread, because nothing here was watching the page.
The probe reports that a post exists. It never reads scores: turning a post into rows means
deciding which published label belongs in which catalog column, and that is judgement.
Two modes, feed first. A feed is a data file — no JavaScript, no bot challenge, no layout to
break — and it beat the browser on the two sites that block one. `render` drives headless
Chrome and is only for makers who publish no feed.
`verdict` records what was measured on 2026-08-05, so an unreadable source is not

`verdict` records what was measured on 2026-08-05, so an unreadable source is not re-investigated by every person who opens this file. Three of these have no working path and one has none yet, and saying so is the point: a blank entry reads as "nobody tried".

pages.verdict: Feed works. The HTML index does not: headless Chrome gets Cloudflare's 'Just a moment...' interstitial and zero links. Do not switch this one to render. The feed also carries /academy/ course pages, so it is filtered to /index/, where launches live.
RSS 2.0, valid. Covers the DeepMind side; Gemini announcements sometimes also appear on blog.google, which this does not watch.
No feed at /rss.xml or /news/rss.xml (both 404). The HTML index renders and lists posts.
GitHub Pages site renders; /index.xml is 404 so there is no feed to prefer.
Renders. rss.xml does not resolve at all (connection failure, not 404).

NO PATH. The index renders to 728 characters and one cookie link — the post list never arrives without interaction. A *post* page renders fine, which is how batch 17 was captured, so the id has to come from somewhere else: the namespace watch in report:gaps sees a new Qwen model the day it is served, and the release post is then at https://qwen.ai/blog?id=<family>. The qwenlm.github.io feed is a trap: it parses, it has 44 entries, and its newest post is Qwen3Guard — it stopped mirroring a generation ago, exactly like lmarena/arena-catalog.
NO PATH, re-checked 2026-08-05. The docs site renders to 314 characters of navigation; /rss.xml and /news/rss return 200 with no items, and github.com/deepseek-ai.atom carries no entries either.
NO PATH, re-checked 2026-08-05. Cloudflare challenges the browser and returns 403 for /news/rss.xml, /rss.xml and /blog/rss.xml alike. Both doors are shut and neither is a URL problem.

NO PATH, re-checked 2026-08-05. z.ai/blog is 404 and the root renders to 153 characters of app shell whose only links are the terms of service and the privacy policy — it is a product surface, not a publication one. /rss.xml, /blog/index.xml and docs.z.ai/rss.xml are all 404. GLM releases have to be found another way; the namespace watch still sees them the day a provider serves them.

No feed at /blog/rss/ or /blog/feed/ (both 404). The index renders and lists posts; the top item on 2026-08-05 was Introducing Muse Spark 1.1, which is a catalog model, so this is a live surface and not an archive.
Feed at /index.xml (7 entries). /blog/rss.xml and /feed.xml are 404 — the Hugo default path is the one that works.
